claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: 11.6 km actually driven against a 9.8 km recommended route is a deviation of 1.80 km, well outside the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. This is not a within-tolerance trip that can be waved through.

The GPS trace corroborates which route was taken and when, exactly the use POL-RD-22 permits: the map-matched fixes run on Upper Bukit Timah Road and Bukit Timah Road to 18:44:00, move onto Holland Road from 18:44:30, continue via Napier Road, and only rejoin the recommended line on Kim Seng Road at about 18:58. The diversion is a real, mapped detour, not a measurement artefact.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The only traffic record in the case is LTA advisory LTA-TI-260914-6951, a road closure on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road, and its active window is 00:30 to 05:30 on 14 September 2026. This trip ran from 18:29 to 19:00 that evening. The advisory's window does not overlap the trip window, so POL-RD-23's requirement of a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route AND overlaps the trip window is not met.

POL-RD-23 is express that a driver's assertion of traffic, with no such data for the recommended segment at the trip time, does not justify the reroute. That is this case: the closure on the record had ended about thirteen hours before the trip; the trace shows the vehicle moving along Bukit Timah Road at reported speeds of 19 to 32 km/h up to the deviation point, consistent with a road that was open and flowing; and the rider's statement on file is that the road was open and moving. The driver's 'LTA announced it, so I took Holland Road' cannot supply the justification the advisory withholds.

The facts select POL-RD-24(d): the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, 1.80 km at 0.72 SGD/km, which the fare ledger itself carries as excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.30; and the ledger shows exactly that 1.30 already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 1.30), matching the trip record's fare_adjusted event. The matrix sends that money to the rider, not back to the driver.

No row of the POL-RD-24 matrix yields a payment to the driver. Rows (a) and (c) both require traffic justification, which the advisory defeats; rows (b) and (d) direct the excess distance fare to the rider; and row (e) is unavailable because the deviation is over 1 km. The driver's claim to have the 1.30 SGD restored to him therefore finds no row of the matrix to stand on.

I do not dispute the notification limb. The driver's in-app message at 18:41:22 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?') preceded the departure from the recommended line at 18:44, and the rider answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, so on POL-RD-21's terms the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment.

Notification and acknowledgment do not carry the driver into row (a). Row (a) requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as informed and agreed, and POL-RD-24's not-justified branch contains no information element at all: row (d) turns on justification and distance alone. The rider's 'ok sure' was in any event given in answer to the driver's assertion that the road was closed, a premise the traffic record contradicts for the trip time, so it cannot be treated as an informed agreement to a reroute the driver had no traffic basis for.

This dispute is for the AI to decide, not to escalate: the contested amount is 1.30 SGD, far below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence subject only to POL-RD-25's 0.80 floor, which COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 support; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so no raised confidence threshold applies; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in this policy version (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false), so the 1.80 km deviation does not take the case out of AI decision.

claims.text: The driver satisfied POL-RD-21 on this record. He sent the rider an in-app chat at 18:41:22 — before the route deviation detected at 18:44:22 — with the brief reason the clause requires ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?'); the rider read it (read_at 18:42:30) and replied 'ok sure' at 18:41:47. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and that is exactly what this log shows.

The only traffic artifact in the record names a ROAD_CLOSURE on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road and prescribes 'Diversion via Holland Rd' — the very recommended corridor the driver left at 18:44:22 and the very alternate he took, the GPS fixes placing the vehicle on Holland Road from 18:44:30. The driver's account therefore tracks LTA's own published corridor and diversion, while the rider's denial that any closure was announced is supported by nothing in the record. I do not overstate it: the advisory's active window (00:30–05:30) does not overlap the trip window (18:34–19:00), so POL-RD-23's strict data test is not met on its face, and this artifact's force is corroboration of the driver's good faith rather than a dispositive justification.

The rider's counterparty statement — that the road was open and that she agreed 'only because he said it was closed' — is a bare assertion made the morning after the refund. The contemporaneous chat log carries admissibility weight 1.0 with no issue codes, is complete and untruncated, and records an unqualified 'ok sure' given after she had read the driver's specific question. Under POL-RD-21 the acknowledgment the chat log carries governs whether the deviation was agreed, and the rider's later, uncorroborated denial does not displace it.

On any view of the matrix the driver's exposure is capped, and it has already been met. POL-RD-24 provides exactly one refund where a deviation is not traffic-justified and exceeds tolerance — the excess distance fare — which here is the deviation of 1.80 km (POL-RD-22: recorded actual 11.6 km minus recommended 9.8 km) times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, with no surge applied: 1.30 SGD. That is precisely the figure already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so nothing further can lawfully be taken from him, and neither POL-RD-24 nor any other clause permits any part of the trip fare itself, or any larger sum, to be recovered.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a route-deviation dispute under POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION (v2.1 s.1.3-1.4).

Facts. The platform's own recorded distances give a deviation of 1.80 km (POL-RD-22, v2.1 1.4): 11.6 km actually driven against a 9.8 km recommended route. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05020) shows which route was taken — Upper Bukit Timah Road and Bukit Timah Road to 18:44, then Holland Road, Napier Road and Kim Seng Road, rejoining the recommended line at about 18:58 — and, as POL-RD-22 directs, is not used to re-measure distance. 1.80 km is over the 1.0 km tolerance.

Traffic justification. POL-RD-23 requires a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route AND overlaps the trip window. The only traffic record (EV-ADVIS-05020-01, LTA-TI-260914-6951) is a Bukit Timah Road closure (towards City, between Farrer Road and Cluny Road) with an active window of 00:30-05:30 on 14 September 2026; the trip ran 18:34-19:00. The window does not overlap the trip, so the reroute is not traffic-justified. The driver's assertion of a closure does not supply what the traffic data withholds, and the rider's later statement that the road was open need not be weighed — the advisory disposes of the point for the trip time.

Refund matrix. POL-RD-24 (v2.1 1.3) row (d) applies: not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is 1.80 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.30 SGD, without surge, and the fare ledger (EV-FARE-05020) already records 1.30 SGD refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, matching the trip record's fare_adjusted event).

The driver's in-app notice at 18:41:22 and the rider's 'ok sure' reply at 18:41:47 (POL-RD-21, EV-CHAT-05020) are on the record, but they do not change the outcome: row (a) needs traffic justification as well, and row (d) turns on justification and distance alone. No row of the matrix pays the driver, so his request to have the 1.30 SGD restored is not supported and the refund of 1.30 SGD stands; the driver's point that his exposure is capped at the excess distance fare (1.30 SGD) is correct and is the figure used.

Confidence and forum. The deciding facts rest on EV-TRIP-05020, EV-ADVIS-05020-01 and EV-FARE-05020, each at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0. POL-RD-25 sets the bar at 0.80, and POL-GEN-22 makes the ruling final at this value (the amount contested is 1.30 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0; POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in this policy version). No referral and no escalation applies.

What the record shows. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-05020) gives 11.6 km driven against a 9.8 km recommended route — a deviation of 1.80 km, computed the way POL-RD-22 directs (actual minus recommended, the recorded distances). That is above the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05020) shows the vehicle leaving the recommended line at Bukit Timah Road / Farrer Road around 18:44 and rejoining at Kim Seng Road around 18:58, so the Holland Road detour is real and mapped, not a measurement artefact.

Traffic justification fails (POL-RD-23). A reroute is traffic-justified only where a traffic advisory intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The only advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-05020-01) is an LTA road closure on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road that ran 00:30–05:30 on 14 September. This trip ran 18:34–19:00 that evening; the advisory's window does not overlap the trip window and the artifact itself records justifies_reroute false. The driver's argument that the advisory shows LTA published a Holland Road diversion is the driver's good faith, but POL-RD-23's data test is not met, and a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data for the trip time does not justify the reroute. The rider's account that the road was open and moving is consistent with the trace, which shows traffic on Bukit Timah Road running at 19–32 km/h up to the deviation point.

Notification (POL-RD-21) was satisfied, but it does not change the result. The driver did message in-app at 18:41:22, before the deviation, with the brief reason, and the rider read it and answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47 — so the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment. That limb matters only to row (a) of the POL-RD-24 matrix, which also requires traffic justification. With justification absent, row (d) applies, and row (d) turns on justification and distance alone; the rider's later statement that she agreed only because the driver said the road was closed does not alter that, because agreement is not an element of row (d).

The amount. POL-RD-24(d) refunds the excess distance fare in full: the 1.80 km deviation times the $0.72 per-km rate carried by the fare ledger (EV-FARE-05020), with no surge, which is $1.30. The driver's own submission that his exposure is capped at $1.30 is correct, and the rider's position that the matrix sends that money to the rider is also correct — 1.80 × 0.72 = 1.30, and the ledger already shows refund_issued_sgd 1.30 with payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, matching the fare_adjusted event. No row of the matrix pays anything to the driver, and no part of the trip fare itself, or any larger sum, can be recovered from him.

Neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no raised threshold applies, and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in this policy version. No clause of this dispute produces a referral. The $1.30 refund stands as the correct outcome of the route deviation.

ruling.explanation:
To Mr D-59361 (driver) and Ms R-78242 (rider), on trip TRP-05020.

What the record shows. The recommended route was 9.8 km; the vehicle covered 11.6 km. Under POL-RD-22 (v2.1 1.4) that is a deviation of 1.80 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance, and the GPS trace confirms the vehicle left the recommended line at Bukit Timah Road/Farrer Road at 18:44 and rejoined at Kim Seng Road at about 18:58.

Was the reroute justified by traffic? No. POL-RD-23 (v2.1 1.4) requires an LTA advisory for the recommended route that overlaps the trip time. The only advisory on file, LTA-TI-260914-6951, is a closure on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road valid 00:30-05:30 on 14 September; this trip ran 18:34-19:00, so the window does not overlap. An advisory that had ended about thirteen hours before the trip cannot justify the reroute, and the driver's account that LTA had announced a closure cannot stand in for data covering the trip time.

Which row of the POL-RD-24 (v2.1 1.3) matrix applies. Row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km. The excess distance fare goes back to the rider in full - 1.80 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.30 SGD, with no surge. That is exactly the 1.30 SGD the fare ledger shows already refunded to Ms R-78242 and recovered from Mr D-59361.

The driver's arguments, answered. ruling.explanation:
Driver and rider — the route facts are not in dispute and the money follows from them.

The platform's own trip record (EV-TRIP-05020) shows 11.6 km driven against a 9.8 km recommended route. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is 11.6 − 9.8 = 1.80 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance, so this is not a within-tolerance trip. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05020) confirms which route was taken — the vehicle left Bukit Timah Road for Holland Road at about 18:44 and rejoined at Kim Seng Road — and is used for that, not to re-measure distance.

Traffic justification fails on POL-RD-23. The only traffic record is LTA advisory LTA-TI-260914-6951 (EV-ADVIS-05020-01), a Bukit Timah Road closure between Farrer Road and Cluny Road, but its active window is 00:30–05:30 on 14 September 2026 while this trip ran 18:34–19:00. The advisory does not overlap the trip window, so it cannot justify the reroute, and a driver's assertion of traffic without such data does not either.

Your notification duty, driver, was met: the chat log (EV-CHAT-05020) shows your 18:41:22 message asking about the Holland Road diversion and the rider's 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, before the deviation at 18:44 — on POL-RD-21 the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment. But notification does not decide the money. POL-RD-24's not-justified branch turns on justification and distance alone; row (a)'s no-refund outcome needs traffic justification as well, and that is absent.

POL-RD-24 therefore selects row (d): not traffic-justified and deviation over 1 km, the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is 1.80 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.30 SGD (POL-RD-22, POL-RD-24). The fare ledger (EV-FARE-05020) already carries exactly that — excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.30, refund_issued_sgd 1.30, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED — matching the trip record's fare_adjusted event. No row of POL-RD-24 pays the driver anything, and nothing in the policy lets a larger sum be recovered or the trip fare itself be touched.

Because the matrix sends the 1.30 SGD to the rider and that is already the state of the account, your request, driver, to have the 1.30 SGD restored to you is not supported and the present state stands.

The AI may decide this: the contested amount is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence, subject to POL-RD-25's 0.80 floor, which the complete weight-1.0 artifacts meet; both profiles show fraud_flags 0, and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false). The rider's later statement that the road was open does not change the outcome: the result follows the recorded distances and the advisory's window. No clause produces a referral in this case.

ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: 11.6 km actually driven against a 9.8 km recommended route is a deviation of 1.80 km, well outside the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. This is not a within-tolerance trip that can be waved through.

The GPS trace corroborates which route was taken and when, exactly the use POL-RD-22 permits: the map-matched fixes run on Upper Bukit Timah Road and Bukit Timah Road to 18:44:00, move onto Holland Road from 18:44:30, continue via Napier Road, and only rejoin the recommended line on Kim Seng Road at about 18:58. The diversion is a real, mapped detour, not a measurement artefact.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The only traffic record in the case is LTA advisory LTA-TI-260914-6951, a road closure on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road, and its active window is 00:30 to 05:30 on 14 September 2026. This trip ran from 18:29 to 19:00 that evening. The advisory's window does not overlap the trip window, so POL-RD-23's requirement of a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route AND overlaps the trip window is not met.

POL-RD-23 is express that a driver's assertion of traffic, with no such data for the recommended segment at the trip time, does not justify the reroute. That is this case: the closure on the record had ended about thirteen hours before the trip; the trace shows the vehicle moving along Bukit Timah Road at reported speeds of 19 to 32 km/h up to the deviation point, consistent with a road that was open and flowing; and the rider's statement on file is that the road was open and moving. The driver's 'LTA announced it, so I took Holland Road' cannot supply the justification the advisory withholds.

The facts select POL-RD-24(d): the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, 1.80 km at 0.72 SGD/km, which the fare ledger itself carries as excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.30; and the ledger shows exactly that 1.30 already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 1.30), matching the trip record's fare_adjusted event. The matrix sends that money to the rider, not back to the driver.

No row of the POL-RD-24 matrix yields a payment to the driver. Rows (a) and (c) both require traffic justification, which the advisory defeats; rows (b) and (d) direct the excess distance fare to the rider; and row (e) is unavailable because the deviation is over 1 km. The driver's claim to have the 1.30 SGD restored to him therefore finds no row of the matrix to stand on.

I do not dispute the notification limb. The driver's in-app message at 18:41:22 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?') preceded the departure from the recommended line at 18:44, and the rider answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, so on POL-RD-21's terms the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment.

Notification and acknowledgment do not carry the driver into row (a). Row (a) requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as informed and agreed, and POL-RD-24's not-justified branch contains no information element at all: row (d) turns on justification and distance alone. The rider's 'ok sure' was in any event given in answer to the driver's assertion that the road was closed, a premise the traffic record contradicts for the trip time, so it cannot be treated as an informed agreement to a reroute the driver had no traffic basis for.

This dispute is for the AI to decide, not to escalate: the contested amount is 1.30 SGD, far below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence subject only to POL-RD-25's 0.80 floor, which COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 support; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so no raised confidence threshold applies; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in this policy version (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false), so the 1.80 km deviation does not take the case out of AI decision.

The driver satisfied POL-RD-21 on this record. He sent the rider an in-app chat at 18:41:22 — before the route deviation detected at 18:44:22 — with the brief reason the clause requires ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?'); the rider read it (read_at 18:42:30) and replied 'ok sure' at 18:41:47. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and that is exactly what this log shows.

The only traffic artifact in the record names a ROAD_CLOSURE on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road and prescribes 'Diversion via Holland Rd' — the very recommended corridor the driver left at 18:44:22 and the very alternate he took, the GPS fixes placing the vehicle on Holland Road from 18:44:30. The driver's account therefore tracks LTA's own published corridor and diversion, while the rider's denial that any closure was announced is supported by nothing in the record. I do not overstate it: the advisory's active window (00:30–05:30) does not overlap the trip window (18:34–19:00), so POL-RD-23's strict data test is not met on its face, and this artifact's force is corroboration of the driver's good faith rather than a dispositive justification.

The rider's counterparty statement — that the road was open and that she agreed 'only because he said it was closed' — is a bare assertion made the morning after the refund. The contemporaneous chat log carries admissibility weight 1.0 with no issue codes, is complete and untruncated, and records an unqualified 'ok sure' given after she had read the driver's specific question. Under POL-RD-21 the acknowledgment the chat log carries governs whether the deviation was agreed, and the rider's later, uncorroborated denial does not displace it.

On any view of the matrix the driver's exposure is capped, and it has already been met. POL-RD-24 provides exactly one refund where a deviation is not traffic-justified and exceeds tolerance — the excess distance fare — which here is the deviation of 1.80 km (POL-RD-22: recorded actual 11.6 km minus recommended 9.8 km) times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, with no surge applied: 1.30 SGD.
